summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 6 upside misses — G24.DE +6%, EXPN.L +5%, SGE.L +5%, RHM.DE +5%, SN.L +4%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (ASM.AS -9%, CCC.L -7%, BESI.AS -6%, ASML.AS -6%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: ASM.AS (-8.52%) — No confirmed company-specific news found for 2026-10-16; searches returned only older coverage. The -8.5% move is likely a semicap sector sell-off tied to mid-October ASML/peer results, which I could not verify. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: ASM.AS is a Dutch mid/large-cap semiconductor-equipment name that no strategy lists. Even if it were in scope, an -8.5% sector-driven gap-down would likely fail momentum and gap filters, and the bot is probably long-only.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for Scout24 (G24.DE), the German classifieds platform. The searches turned up nothing dated 2026-10-16, so this is likely a rebound or a sector or software-wide move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: G24.DE is a mid-cap German (MDAX-class) internet/classifieds name that no strategy lists. With no identifiable catalyst, a news-reactive trigger would also have had nothing to fire on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a small 'EU mid-cap momentum' watchlist (e.g. MDAX/SDAX names above a ~€5B cap and a €20M average daily volume floor). Let it enter on a gap or day move of ≥ +4% with volume ≥ 1.5× its 20-day average.

top_movers.suggestion: Add a sector-relative rebound screen that adds FTSE 100 names to the mean-reversion universe when they are ≥15% below their 200-day MA and a peer basket (Sage, Auto Trader) gaps up ≥3% by the open.
